annotations.description: Chose green for Thriving Isle's additional color, but the deck appears to have more black cards (Deadly Plot, Gravedigger, Necromancer's Stockpile) than green cards (Dwynen's Elite). Black would likely provide access to more castable spells drawn later.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Green as the additional color for Thriving Isle
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black as the additional color for Thriving Isle, since the deck appears to have more black cards that would benefit from the mana fixing

annotations.description: Player bottomed Teferi's Tutelage instead of the redundant Island during scry 2. Teferi's Tutelage has exceptional synergy with Bruvac the Grandiloquent already in hand (every draw would mill opponent for 4 cards). The player already has 3 Islands in hand and doesn't need another land.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Teferi's Tutelage on the bottom of library, keeping Island on top
annotations.betterLine: Put Island on the bottom, keeping Teferi's Tutelage on top to draw next turn. Teferi's Tutelage + Bruvac is a powerful mill engine and the player is already flooded with lands.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Bruvac the Grandiloquent but the mana payment failed and the cast was rolled back, wasting the priority window. Additionally, Bruvac's mill-doubling ability is largely irrelevant in this game state with no mill effects available, making it a vanilla 1/4 for 3 mana. Activating Teferi's Protege to loot would have been productive regardless of mana issues.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Bruvac the Grandiloquent with an invalid mana plan, resulting in a rollback and no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Teferi's Protege to draw and discard, digging for better cards, then potentially cast Bruvac with remaining mana if the payment works (though with Protege tapped, only 3 mana from lands would remain which should suffice for Bruvac's {2}{U} cost).

annotations.description: Casting Tolarian Kraken taps out completely when Bruvac the Grandiloquent would cost only 3 mana, synergize powerfully with Belltower Sphinx already on board (doubling mill triggers), and leave 3 mana open for Sweep Away to answer the opponent's developing board (Lord of the Accursed threatening menace for zombies).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tolarian Kraken for 6 mana, tapping out completely
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bruvac the Grandiloquent for 3 mana, establishing a mill engine with Belltower Sphinx while holding up Sweep Away to bounce Lord of the Accursed or other threats

annotations.description: Cast Deadly Plot before playing the Swamp from hand. Should always play the land first to maximize available mana and flexibility. With the Swamp played first, they'd have 6 mana instead of 5, leaving 2 mana after Deadly Plot instead of 1 - potentially relevant for Necromancer's Stockpile activation ({1}{B}) or Lord of the Accursed activation ({1}{B}).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Deadly Plot before playing Swamp land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Deadly Plot. This leaves 2 mana open (including {B}) which enables Necromancer's Stockpile activation or Lord of the Accursed's menace ability if needed.

annotations.description: Passed on activating Necromancer's Stockpile during combat with 2 untapped lands (Forest + Swamp) and creature cards in hand. Could have discarded Elvish Rejuvenator to draw a card at instant speed with the opponent fully tapped out. The mana would otherwise go unused since neither Gravedigger (3B) nor Rejuvenator (2G) can be cast with only 2 available mana post-combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Necromancer's Stockpile
annotations.betterLine: Activate Necromancer's Stockpile discarding Elvish Rejuvenator to draw a card, since the 2 mana available cannot cast either hand card this turn anyway, making this essentially free card filtering.

annotations.description: Passed on activating Necromancer's Stockpile to discard Gravedigger (a Zombie) during combat. This would have drawn a card and created a 2/2 Zombie token that would be a 3/3 with Lord of the Accursed's buff, representing significant value. The Gravedigger's recursion target (Reckless Amplimancer) is relatively low-value compared to getting a 3/3 body + card draw immediately.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Necromancer's Stockpile
annotations.betterLine: Activate Necromancer's Stockpile discarding Gravedigger to draw a card and create a 2/2 Zombie token (3/3 with Lord of the Accursed), gaining both board presence and card advantage

annotations.description: Attacking with Bruvac the Grandiloquent risks losing the key mill-doubling legendary creature for just 1 point of damage. The opponent has sick creatures (Elderleaf Mentor 3/2, Elf Warrior 1/1, Zombie Token 3/3) that can block, and a double-block would deal 4 damage to Bruvac's 4 toughness, killing it. While Sweep Away could save it, using a removal spell reactively to protect an unnecessary attack is wasteful.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Belltower Sphinx and Bruvac the Grandiloquent
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Belltower Sphinx (which has flying and is safe). Keep Bruvac back as a blocker and protect the mill-doubling engine. The 1 damage from Bruvac is not worth the risk of losing the deck's key synergy piece.

annotations.description: With exactly 6 mana available (4 Forests, 2 Swamps), casting Suspicious Shambler (3B) uses only 4 mana and deploys a single 4/2 body (5/3 with Lord). Instead, casting both Crow of Dark Tidings (2B) and Elvish Rejuvenator (2G) would use all 6 mana to deploy two creatures - including a flying Zombie that becomes 3/2 with Lord, plus land ramp from Rejuvenator. Two bodies provide more board presence, evasion damage, and mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Suspicious Shambler (3B) for a single 5/3 Zombie with Lord
annotations.betterLine: Cast both Crow of Dark Tidings (2B, flying Zombie) and Elvish Rejuvenator (2G) to deploy two creatures, get a flyer, and potentially ramp a land - using all 6 available mana efficiently

annotations.description: Passed on activating Necromancer's Stockpile to discard Crow of Dark Tidings (a Zombie), which would have drawn a card and created a 2/2 Zombie token (effectively 3/3 with Lord of the Accursed). This is significant value — card replacement plus a relevant body — all for just {1}{B} and a discard. The opponent has no untapped blockers, so the new token could even attack next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating anything in precombat main.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Necromancer's Stockpile, discarding Crow of Dark Tidings to draw a card and create a 3/3 Zombie token (2/2 + Lord of the Accursed buff), then proceed to combat.
